title: Fixing legal citation errors on Mac: a guide for paralegals in 2026
metaTitle: Stop legal citation errors: proofreading tips for paralegals on Mac
description: Learn how to catch and fix legal citation errors on your Mac. Practical strategies for paralegals to improve document accuracy and reduce revision time.
intro: Legal citation errors can derail your filings and damage your firm's professional reputation. Catching these mistakes requires a structured approach to proofreading that goes beyond standard spellcheck tools on your Mac.
tldr: Legal citation errors are common due to high document volumes and cognitive fatigue.
Manual proofreading is prone to the self-editing bias where your brain skips over mistakes.
Changing your medium, reading aloud, and using specialized software are effective ways to improve accuracy.
Lazur helps by providing a quick way to check formatting and dictate corrections directly in your legal documents.

blocks.text: Legal citation errors often occur because of the sheer volume of material paralegals handle. When you work on 20 to 50 cases simultaneously, your focus shifts rapidly. This context switching leaves little room for deep, line-by-line verification. Your brain naturally fills in what it expects to see rather than what is actually written on the screen.

Cognitive load is another major factor. Legal writing is dense and complex. When you are busy parsing arguments or checking facts, your working memory hits a limit. Mundane details like a missing period in a citation or an incorrect court abbreviation become invisible to you. This is known as the self-editing bias.

The costs of these errors extend far beyond a quick fix. They include lost billable time for corrections, diminished credibility with opposing counsel, and potential frustration for judges. A document riddled with errors suggests a lack of attention to detail, which can impact how your firm is perceived by clients.

items: Print your document. Reading on paper forces your brain to process text differently than reading on a screen.
Read your work aloud. This technique forces you to slow down and hear the rhythm of your sentences, which helps catch awkward phrasing and missing words.
Use a checklist. Break down your proofreading into distinct passes. Check for citations first, then grammar, then formatting.
Use a second set of eyes. Whenever possible, have a colleague review your work. This is the most reliable way to catch errors you have become blind to.

faq.question: How can I stop making citation errors?
faq.answer: Focus on one type of error at a time, read your work aloud, and use specialized tools like PerfectIt or Lexis for Microsoft Office to supplement your manual review.
